name: Keimyung University
overview:
Keimyung University (abbreviated KMU) is located in Daegu, the 4th largest city in South Korea in terms of inhabitants (over 2.5 million).


Daegu is an hour and a half from Seoul by KTX (express train). It is a true college town.


KMU was founded in 1954 and has become one of the most prestigious private universities outside of Seoul.


It maintains very close relations with more than 226 universities and organizations in 46 countries around the world, which makes it the university with the most extensive international exchange network in the country.


It also welcomes 27,000 students from around the world on three different campuses:

  1. Seongseo – just over 1.8 km² (most courses, student residences, and the main library are located here)
  2. Daemyung – located in the city center
  3. Dongsan – also in the city center, home to Dongsan Hospital


The Seongseo library benefits from very sophisticated multimedia equipment.
administrative:
1. Application dossier


Once nominated by the Epitech IAFF team at Keimyung University, you will receive an email about the application process from Keimyung University.

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.


Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • ID photo (3.5 x 4.5 cm with a white background)
  • Passport color copy
  • Epitech transcripts in English
  • Recommendation letter in English
  • Medical form completed
  • Agreement on personal information form completed


*If you are a non-EU student, some additional documents may be requested for your Korean visa application. A bank certificate in English may be required and it must clearly state the USD equivalent of your bank balance showing a minimum of $20,000. The required amount is subject to change according to the actual cost of living each year.


If your financial statement is not in your name, you must attach a letter from the account holder, indicating their relationship to you and stating that they will be financially responsible for your stay at KMU.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Acceptation by KMU


Your host university will review your application and then send you the three documents needed for the visa application:

  • Certificate of Business Registration
  • Certificate of Admission (COA)
  • Certificate of Exchange Student


3. Visa and ARC (more information here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.


If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2026 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€ (please note that the visa fee may change every 6 months)
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • You may be asked to send the following documents : valid passport, certificate of admission, business registration of the host university, completed visa application form, recent certificate of school record, verification of bank account balance, visa processing fee
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4.Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open.


Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. The test can be conducted in Korea, and in the form of a skin test, blood test, or X-ray. You'll need to bring the original test result to the dormitory move-in.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.


All the information for exchange students is available here.


You can create a Korean bank account at iMBank on campus.


Please install KakaoTalk before arriving and bring cash.


6.Campus life


You will be part of a buddy program – your local buddy will help you with administrative tasks and other daily needs. You can join clubs during the first week (literature, drawing, sports, English conversations, etc.). You can also buy university jackets. There are a lot of food places on campus.

Facilities include:

  • Reading room and seminar room
  • Lounge with Internet access
  • Shower room and washing space. Hot water is provided from 6:00 a.m. - 9:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. - 11:00 p.m.
  • Laundry Machine In addition, central reading room, fitness center, table tennis courts, and store are housed in the Administration Building. There is a multi-purpose outdoor playground for soccer, baseball, etc.


Notes:

  • Dormitory fees may vary each semester.
  • Students are strongly encouraged to transfer money from a bank in their country or with the WISE service during the payment period. Please note that making a payment with a credit card is not available.
  • A tuberculosis test is mandatory for the students who stay in the dorm. Students need to take the test before they come to Korea (within 6 months) if they stay in a dormitory. The test result must be in English or Korean.


Off-campus accommodation


You can also choose to live by yourself in a shared apartment with roommates or a studio. Former Epitech students who went to KMU can add you to a Discord server with real estate agent recommendations.
courses:
Credits


Number of local credits to be earned per year: 30 (not counting EIP credits)

Number of local credits to be earned per semester: 15


Academic calendar


Fall semester: From early September to end of December

Spring semester: From early March to end of June


Department and Courses


You will have the opportunity to study on two campuses: Daemyung and Seongseo, 20 minutes from the city center (where most classes are held).


Most classes share the same time slot, and some are held in different buildings, making it difficult to attend multiple classes in a timely manner. Therefore, pay attention to the class schedule and location when registering.


Class registration is on a first come, first served basis, often occurs early in the morning (European time) and fills up quickly due to limited space. We recommend staying awake or waking up early to secure your preferred classes.


It is advisable to register for all desired courses and drop any unsuitable ones during the course drop-out period.


  1. Epitech students following the non-certificate program will be enrolled in the Department of Game & Mobile Engineering.


You will have to choose your classes as follows:

  • Option 1: 3 computer classes, 1 Korean class, 1 elective class (non-computer)
  • Option 2: 4 computer classes and 1 Korean class
  • Computer classes must be at the 3rd and 4th year level
  • Business classes, Korean language, and Korean culture classes are at the 1st year level


The list of elective classes will be communicated to you by the university.


The classes validated by Epitech are the following:


Semester 1:

  • 3D Game Authoring Practice (3D Game Design) – 3 local credits
  • Mobile Applications Development (Smart Phone Applications) – 3 local credits
  • 3D Game Basic (Next Generation Game Technology) – 3 local credits
  • Computer Graphics 2 – 3 local credits
  • 3D Asset Modeling – 3 local credits
  • Human Computer Interaction (HCI) – 3 local credits
  • Game Project 1 – 3 local credits
  • Project II – 3 local credits
  • Korean Language Practice – 4 local credits


Semester 2:

  • Computer Graphics 1 – 3 local credits
  • Game Project 2 (Advanced C / C++) – 3 local credits
  • Fundamentals of Game Development – 3 local credits
  • 3D Game Applications – 3 local credits
  • Mobile Game Programming – 3 local credits
  • Character Modeling – 3 local credits
  • Korean Language Practice – 4 local credits


2.For students choosing the certificate program, you will be enrolled in the Department of Big Data Management


The classes validated by Epitech are the following (more information here):

  • Cybersecurity
  • AI & Soft Skills
  • (Course Materials: Textbook "Business Statistics, A First Course, 7th Edition", David M. Levine, Kathryn A. Szabat, David F. Stephan)
  • Statistical Data Analysis
  • (Course Materials: Same as above)
  • Digital Transformation
  • Motion Learning
  • IT Management
  • Business Programming
  • (Prerequisites: Basic Algebra)


Course Format and Workload


The classes are mainly between Epitech students.


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)


  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses


  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Visa: 126€
  • ARC: 20€
  • Insurance from university: 70€/month
  • Additional Insurance: 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Books and other supplies: 120€
  • Administrative fees and other expenses: at least 800yuan in cash (100€) according to a former student (2024-2025), etc.


Estimated monthly budget


The local currency is the Won. 1 € = 1667,19 KRW (rate as of October 2025).


Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


You should plan a budget of about 600€ a month, excluding rent.


Housing : about 300€ or less (if you live with roommates) / Former students (2024-2025) paid about 120€ for an apartment with roommates.


Food : maximum 300€


Transportation : Rechargeable T-money card: 35€


In Daegu

  • Metro: about 1€
  • Bus: about 1€

In Seoul

  • Metro: 0.7 to 1.20€
  • Bus: 0.8 to 2€


Monthly Climate card: 40€


Phone, internet : 12€ for unlimited 5G

  • Please note that if you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes 35G data in South Korea.
  • Former students (2024-2025) have recommended Chingu Mobile.


Leisure : 100€+


These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Your visa allows you to work in South Korea up to 20 hours a week, Monday to Friday, during your study stay. However, to be able to work, you must change your visa to an S3 on site. Please note that it is still very difficult for a foreigner who does not speak Korean to find a part-time job. Student jobs through KMU include: English teacher, French teacher, Language advisory support.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut. You'll be able to create a bank account in South Korea only when you have your ARC.
  • Useful apps: Coupang and Karrot (online shopping - equivalents of Amazon and Leboncoin), KakaoTalk and Google Translate/Papago/Deepl (communication), Baemin and Ubereats (food delivery), Uber, Naevar/Kakao maps because Google maps doesn't work (transport)
  • Use the Kakao Subway app, very useful for navigating Seoul’s subway. You can buy a metro card at a 7/11 or C&U (your student or bank card may also be used after about a month).
  • It is not compulsory to get a SIM card, as free wifi is often available in the streets. However, SIM cards provide access to more wifi, especially in the subway.
  • Korean people don't really cook and, rather, eat out a lot. You have options like restaurants (like pochas) and convenience stores which are open 24/7. Food is less expensive than in France. Typically, people share a few dishes.
